questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Cardinality of a Finite Set
questions.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $C$ is the number of elements in $C.$ 

Let's start by listing all the elements of $C:$

$$
5,\,10,\,15,\,20,\,25,\,30,\,35,\,40
$$

Since $C$ has $8$ elements, its cardinality is $|C|=\text{8}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Arithmetic Sequences
questions.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
98,\,102,\,106,\,…
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =4 \\  & =102-98 \\  & =106-102 \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =98+(n-1)\cdot 4 \\  & =98+4n-4 \\  & =4n+94.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={4n+94:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4N+94 & =810 \\ 4N & =716 \\ N & =\frac{716}{4} \\ N & =179\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={4n+94:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 179}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $179$ elements, we must have $|A|=179.$

questions.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Geometric Sequences
questions.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
1,\,6,\,36,\,216,\,…
$$

form a geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =6 \\  & =\frac{6}{1} \\  & =\frac{36}{6} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our geometric sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1}=1\cdot {6}^{n-1}={6}^{n-1}.
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
A={{6}^{n-1}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{6}^{N-1} & =2\,176\,782\,336 \\ N-1 & ={log}_{6}⁡(2\,176\,782\,336) \\ N-1 & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡(2\,176\,782\,336)}{{log}_{10}⁡(6)} \\ N-1 & =12 \\ N & =13\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={{6}^{n-1}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 13}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $13$ elements, we must have $|A|=13.$

canonical_examples.problem: What is the cardinal number of $X = \{ a, \emptyset, \{\emptyset\}, \{\{\emptyset\}\}, b \}?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $X$ is the number of elements in $X.$ 

Let's start by listing all the elements of $X{:}$

$$
a, \qquad \emptyset, \qquad \{\emptyset\}, \qquad \{\{\emptyset\}\}, \qquad b
$$

Note the following:

- Only *unique* elements are counted. In other words, duplicate elements are *not* counted separately.

- $\emptyset, \{\emptyset\}$ and $\{\{\emptyset\}\}$ each count as single, distinct elements of $X.$

Since $X$ has $5$ elements, the cardinality is $|X| = 5.$

The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
10, \quad 19, \quad 28,\quad \ldots
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d=9{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =9 \\  & =19-10 \\  & =28-19 \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted $a_n,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =10+(n-1)\cdot 9 \\  & =10+9n-9 \\  & =9n+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={9n+1:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}
$$

where $N\in \mathbb N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}9N+1 & =865 \\ 9N & =864 \\ N & =\frac{864}{9} \\ N & =96\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A = \left\{9n+1: n\in \mathbb N,\: 1\leq n \leq 96  \right\}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $96$ elements, we must have $|A| = 96.$
